messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — two things: what's the expected release cadence for next quarter, and how does oncall handoff work during canaries? Also what's the minimum quality bar for a build to go to canary?

jamal: great Qs. short answer: monthly minor releases + weekly hotfixes.

maria_gonzalez: +1 on clarifying. cadence = "monthly" for minor (feature) releases, with a 2-week feature freeze window. hotfixes as needed, pushed through the fast path.

elaine_cto: to add: canaries are the default rollout for non-security features. canary window is 24-72h depending on traffic. if metrics look good, we promote to full in 1-3 days.

alex: when you say "metrics look good", which exact metrics do we gate on? latency, error rate, QA pass?

maria_gonzalez: primary gates = 95th latency within 1.2x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute, user-facing regressions = zero. also automated smoke tests in CI must pass.

product-ops: do we have a checklist for the freeze window? engineers keep asking which items are mandatory.

sre-oncall-bot: Playbook link: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/release-runbook (updated today) :link:

jamal: Checklist summary (from runbook):
- release notes drafted
- canary config + traffic split defined
- runbooks & rollback plan attached
- perf smoke (+1000 tokens) passed
- QA regression set green
- oncall pager owner assigned for canary window

elaine_cto: Oncall handoff: the owner for the canary window must be explicitly set in the rollout PR description and pinged in #eng-oncall at start time. if an SLA-sensitive route is in the release, escalate to SRE lead before promoting.

alex: good. how do we handle flaky tests discovered after canary starts?

maria_gonzalez: If a flaky test is found post-canary and it affects release quality signals, we pause the promotion, roll back the canary, open a high-priority ticket, and schedule a followup patch. flakey test triage should happen within 4h.

jamal: practical snippet for PR template (paste into PR):

```
Canary window owner: @username
Canary start: yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm UTC
Traffic split: 10% -> 50% over 24h
Rollback plan: revert PR + disable routing
SLA routes impacted: [list]
Smoke test link: <CI job URL>
```

product-ops: will add that to the release checklist doc. thanks.

elaine_cto: one more thing — SLA targets for Dedicated customers are still gated behind legal & ops review. engineering target: make sure releases do not increase P99 latency by more than 10% for SLA routes.

alex: super helpful, thanks. i'll post a short summary to docs and tag folks. :thumbsup:

maria_gonzalez: thank you — I'll host a 30min follow-up office hours tomorrow 10am PT for groups that want clarification. ping me to get the calendar invite.

jamal: marking action items: update PR template, link checklist in runbook, schedule canary owner training.

sre-oncall-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation starts 1918800000.

alex: noted. closing this thread after the office hours — thanks everyone!
